headline: Hybrid Reasoning Agents reports benchmark gains with latent thoughts and text-based tool use
summary: A 13 October arXiv preprint introduces HybridAgents, which alternates between latent internal reasoning and text for tool interaction, with HybridSFT and HybridRL post-training. Across 11 math, science, medicine, search and agentic benchmarks, the authors report that their 8B and 14B systems improve on matched text/latent baselines; they also report 35.5%–54.7% fewer generated tokens, 1.8×–2.6× faster inference and 2.7×–3.7× lower compute cost in their evaluated settings. The paper reports five independent runs for its agentic results and gives average standard deviations and confidence intervals. These are author-reported benchmark results, not independent findings; the paper’s headline aggregates span specific tasks, models, prompts and hardware.
